stories.title: Two Officers Hurt During South End Arrest After Tip Jar Theft, Police Say
stories.dek: Boston police said a Brockton man resisted arrest after a reported larceny at a Harrison Avenue bakery, leaving two officers with non-life-threatening injuries.
body: Two Boston police officers were injured Sunday evening while arresting a man accused of stealing a tip jar from a South End bakery, according to a Boston Police Department release.

Police said an officer from District D-4 responded at about 5:06 p.m. on Oct. 18 to a report of a larceny in progress at 345 Harrison Avenue. Bakery staff told the officer that a person had come into the store, taken a tip jar and left, according to the release. Officers searched the area without finding the person and broadcast a description across the district.

At about 7:30 p.m., officers patrolling near West Fourth Street and Frontage Road saw a man who matched the description, police said. According to the department, the man ran when officers approached, then flailed his arms and actively resisted as several officers stopped him. Officers handcuffed him after repeated verbal commands, the release said.
Two officers were taken to local hospitals with injuries the department described as non-life-threatening.

Police identified the man as Kobe Nevels, 28, of Brockton. He was expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court on charges of larceny from a building, assault and battery on a police officer, and resisting arrest, according to the release. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Suspect Arrested After Resisting Arrest and Injuring Two Officers

stories.title: Hopkinton Man Pleads Not Guilty to Attempted Murder in Lake Maspenock Incident
stories.dek: Prosecutors say a 70-year-old Hopkinton man held a 21-year-old under water at a local beach in June after a dispute over a jet ski.
body: A 70-year-old Hopkinton man pleaded not guilty Monday in Middlesex Superior Court to attempted murder and related charges stemming from a June confrontation at Lake Maspenock, according to the Boston Globe.
Steven A. Dana faces charges of attempted murder, strangulation or suffocation, and misdemeanor assault and battery, the Globe reported. A grand jury indicted him last month.

According to police accounts described in court, the June 3 dispute began over a jet ski. Police allege Dana confronted a group of young people because they did not live in the Hopkinton neighborhood that holds exclusive summer use of the beach's boat ramp. Authorities allege the argument escalated and that Dana slapped a 21-year-old Milford man, pushed him into the water and held him under for about 10 seconds before the man's friends pulled him away. The Globe reported the incident was captured on video.

Police said Dana told them he was the victim and that two of the young men had forced him into the water, and that he repeated that account after learning video existed, according to the Globe. Dana's attorney declined to comment to the newspaper.

Dana was previously arraigned in Framingham District Court and released on $7,500 bail. Judge Michael A. Sullivan approved transferring that bail to the superior court case, and Dana must stay away from the man and the beach and may not possess weapons, the Globe reported. His next pretrial hearing is scheduled for Dec. 11. He is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Hopkinton man arraigned on attempted murder charges for allegedly holding man underwater at lake

stories.title: Abington Woman Pleads Not Guilty to Charges of Abusing Her Infant
stories.dek: A 34-year-old Abington woman was arraigned in Plymouth Superior Court on charges that she seriously injured her 2-month-old daughter.
body: A 34-year-old Abington woman pleaded not guilty Monday in Plymouth Superior Court in Brockton to charges that she physically abused her 2-month-old daughter, according to the Boston Globe.

The woman was indicted Oct. 1 on a felony count of assault and battery on a child causing serious bodily injury and a misdemeanor count of reckless endangerment of a child, the Globe reported. She was arrested in late July after an investigation and had earlier pleaded not guilty in Brockton District Court.

According to the Plymouth District Attorney's office, the woman brought the infant to South Shore Hospital in Weymouth in early July. The baby had a dangerously low body temperature and facial bruising and was flown to the neonatal intensive care unit at Boston Children's Hospital, prosecutors said. A mandated reporter at the hospital alerted authorities, and the DA's office said the infant had serious head injuries consistent with physical abuse.
Prosecutors said in July that the injuries were severe enough that the child may face lasting disabilities.

At Monday's hearing, the woman was ordered to have no contact with an alleged co-defendant and no contact with her daughter unless a Department of Children and Families supervisor or a health care professional requests it, the Globe reported. Her lawyer could not be reached for comment. She is due back in court Nov. 17 and is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Abington woman pleads not guilty to charge she physically abused her 2-month-old baby

stories.title: Beck Plays Two-Dozen-Song Set at MGM Music Hall at Fenway
stories.dek: Beck mixed songs from his new album Ride Lonesome with older favorites at a Saturday show in Fenway, according to a Boston.com review.
body: Beck performed at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on Saturday, Oct. 17, playing a 24-song main set followed by a one-song encore, according to a review and setlist published by Boston.com.

The show came a month after the release of Ride Lonesome, his first album in seven years. Boston.com reviewer Perry Eaton placed the record alongside Beck's earlier stripped-down albums Sea Change and Morning Phase. The set opened with the new single "In the Night" and included the new songs "Slow Canyon" and "Disappearing Act," which the reviewer judged the strongest of the new material.

According to the review, the stage was rearranged throughout the night with minimalist house facades, and heavy reverb shaped much of the sound. The reviewer found the effect sometimes overwhelming but said it gave "The New Pollution" a lounge-like feel. The Mutations-era song "Cold Brains" was singled out as a highlight.

The review said "Think I'm in Love" brought the seated crowd to its feet, and the closing stretch included "Devil's Haircut," "Loser" and "Where It's At." Beck returned alone for an encore cover of Daniel Johnston's "True Love Will Find You in the End."
Los Angeles songwriter Wayne Faler and singer Ioanna Gika opened. Eaton wrote that some of the quieter songs blended together, but concluded that the long set showed Beck's range across eras.

sources.title: Review & setlist: At MGM, Beck brings reverb and rarities, bottles and cans

stories.title: Driver Cited After SUV Strikes Four Parked Cars and Overturns in Allston
stories.dek: Boston police said the driver, who was not injured, did not have a valid license and will be summonsed to Brighton District Court.
body: A driver was cited for operating without a valid license after his SUV struck four parked cars and rolled onto its side on Park Vale Avenue in Allston late Saturday, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.

Officers responded just before midnight to a report of a crash near 4 Park Vale Ave. and found a black GMC Terrain on its driver's side in the middle of the street, police said. The driver had gotten out of the vehicle and stayed at the scene.

According to a preliminary investigation, the GMC hit a parked Honda CR-V, then struck a second parked CR-V and pushed it into a parked Honda Accord. The SUV then rolled over and hit a Nissan Altima parked across the street, police said.

The driver reported no injuries and declined to go to a hospital, according to police. Officers determined he did not have a valid license, and he was cited for unlicensed operation of a motor vehicle and for not having an inspection sticker. The GMC was towed.
The driver, who was not named, will be summonsed to Brighton District Court, Boston.com reported. The department's Auto Investigations Unit is continuing to investigate.

sources.title: Allegedly unlicensed driver hits 4 parked cars, rolls over SUV in Allston crash

stories.title: Woman Shot in Chest Inside Dorchester Apartment Building
stories.dek: Boston police said a woman was wounded at a Washington Street building and that no arrests had been made.
body: A woman was shot in the chest inside an apartment building at 765 Washington St. in Dorchester, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.

Officers responded at about 8 p.m. to a report of a shooting and found the woman with an apparent gunshot wound to the upper left side of her chest, police said. A friend was applying pressure to the wound when officers arrived.

People inside the home told officers that someone from another unit in the three-unit building had fired the shot, according to police. They described the person as wearing a white tank top and blue basketball shorts.

Police said they searched the building but did not find anyone matching that description. Three people from another unit were briefly detained and then released after gunshot residue testing, according to the report.

The woman, whose name and age were not released by police, was taken to Boston Medical Center. Her condition was not stated. No arrests had been made and no suspect had been named, Boston.com reported.

sources.title: Person shot in chest inside Dorchester apartment building

stories.title: Couple in Their 70s Found Dead in Attleboro Home After Fire
stories.dek: Investigators said no working smoke or carbon monoxide alarms were found in the Andover Avenue home and the fire does not appear to have been set intentionally.
body: A couple in their 70s were found dead inside their single-family home on Andover Avenue in Attleboro after a fire on the first floor, according to Boston.com. An earlier version of the Boston.com report misstated the location; the home is in Attleboro.

Attleboro police and firefighters responded around 11:30 a.m. on a Wednesday to 32 Andover Ave., according to the Bristol County District Attorney's Office. Firefighters extinguished a smoldering fire on the first floor, which showed obvious fire damage, the office said.
Responders found a 78-year-old woman and a 76-year-old man on the first floor, and both were pronounced dead at the scene, officials said.

The State Fire Marshal's Office said no working smoke alarms or carbon monoxide detectors were found in the home. State Fire Marshal Jon Davine urged residents to keep working smoke alarms on every level of their homes and noted that smoke from burning modern furnishings is especially toxic.

State Police assigned to the district attorney's office are investigating. Based on the scene examination, witness interviews and other evidence, investigators are focusing on accidental causes and do not believe the fire was intentionally set, the fire marshal's office said. Officials did not state a cause of death.

sources.title: Couple in their 70s found dead in Attleboro home

stories.title: Fire at Somerville Veterans Housing Injures Two, Displaces Residents
stories.dek: Somerville firefighters traced the fire to a lithium-ion battery on an electric skateboard in a basement apartment.
body: A fire at the Massachusetts Bay Veterans Center in Somerville left two people with minor injuries and forced residents from the building, according to the Somerville Fire Department, as reported by Boston.com.

Firefighters responded around 9:35 p.m. Thursday to the building at 2 North St., Boston.com reported. The fire department said the fire was caused by a burning lithium-ion battery on an electric skateboard in a basement apartment.
One occupant and one firefighter suffered minor injuries, according to the department. The basement sustained fire, smoke and water damage, and the rest of the facility had smoke damage.

Gas service to the building was shut off and displaced residents were moved to nearby hotels, the fire department said, without specifying how many people were affected. A resident told Boston.com that about 30 residents were taken to a Somerville hotel, and that he and other upstairs residents were not offered rooms.

The center has 22 transitional and seven permanent housing units for veterans who need supportive services, according to the city of Somerville. The center had not responded to Boston.com's request for comment as of Sunday night.

sources.title: Fire at Somerville veterans housing leaves 2 injured, residents displaced

stories.title: Pedestrian Seriously Injured After Being Struck on Hancock Street in Quincy
stories.dek: Quincy police said a 61-year-old woman suffered life-threatening injuries Saturday night, and the department's crash reconstruction unit is investigating.
body: A 61-year-old woman suffered life-threatening injuries after she was struck by a vehicle on Hancock Street in Quincy late Saturday night, according to a statement the Quincy Police Department posted on Facebook and that Boston.com reported.

Police said they received a call shortly before 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 17 reporting that a pedestrian had been hit near 540 Hancock St. The woman was taken to a Boston-area hospital for treatment, according to the department. Her current condition was not reported.
The vehicle involved was being driven by a 64-year-old Quincy woman, police said. Authorities did not release the name of either the pedestrian or the driver.

Hancock Street was closed to traffic for a period of time while officers worked at the scene. As of Sunday evening, authorities had not said whether the driver would face any charges in connection with the crash, Boston.com reported.
The Quincy Police Department's Crash Reconstruction Unit is leading the investigation into how the crash happened. Police said they would provide updates when more information becomes available.

sources.title: Quincy woman suffers life-threatening injuries after being struck by vehicle

stories.title: Globe Critic Calls Beck's MGM Music Hall Show Detached
stories.dek: A Boston Globe review of Beck's Saturday concert praised his band but found the performance emotionally distant.
body: Beck's Saturday concert at MGM Music Hall at Fenway drew a critical review from the Boston Globe, whose critic James Sullivan described the performance as dispassionate.

The roughly two-hour show featured about 25 songs and leaned on material from Ride Lonesome, the album Beck released in September after a seven-year gap, the longest of his career, according to the review. The set also drew from Mutations, Sea Change and Modern Guilt, along with hits including "Loser" and "Where It's At."

Sullivan noted frequent onstage rearranging between songs, with the band grouped in different formations, including inside a V-shaped scrim. He described the band, which includes longtime collaborators Jason Falkner and Roger Joseph Manning Jr., as excellent, if almost too polished.

The review singled out the new song "For Your Love," which Beck performed alone at a long table facing an empty chair. He closed with a solo acoustic cover of Daniel Johnston's "True Love Will Find You in the End," as he has on this tour, the Globe reported.

Sullivan's central criticism was that Beck's detached delivery, while suited to the melancholy new songs, extended even to his 1990s hits, leaving the evening without much feeling. Wayne Faler and Ioanna Gika were listed as openers.

sources.title: From Beck, a dispassionate display at MGM Music Hall at Fenway

stories.title: Two Women Hospitalized After Early-Morning Shooting in Hyde Park
stories.dek: Boston police said one of the women suffered life-threatening injuries in the shooting on Davidson Street, and no arrests have been made.
body: Two women were taken to the hospital after a shooting on Davidson Street in Hyde Park early Saturday morning, one of them with injuries considered life-threatening, Boston police said, according to the Boston Globe.

Officers were sent to 114 Davidson St. at about 1:12 a.m. on Oct. 17 in response to a radio call, police said. When they arrived, they found two women who had each been struck by gunfire multiple times.

One woman was taken to a local hospital with life-threatening injuries, and the other was taken to a local hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening, according to police. Neither woman was identified.
Police had not announced any arrests or identified any suspects, the Globe reported. Authorities did not describe a possible motive or say what led up to the shooting.
The shooting remains under investigation by Boston police. The Globe said its report would be updated as more information becomes available.

sources.title: Early morning Hyde Park shooting leaves two women hospitalized, one with life-threatening injuries

stories.title: Hyde Park Man Charged With Carrying Loaded Revolver Without License
stories.dek: Boston police said District B-3 officers recovered a loaded revolver from a passenger during an early-morning stop on Delhi Street.
body: Boston police arrested a 24-year-old Hyde Park man early Friday after officers said they found a loaded revolver in his hoodie pocket during a stop in Mattapan, according to a department release.

District B-3 officers patrolling Delhi Street at about 1:16 a.m. on Oct. 16 saw an idling rental vehicle with two people inside and smoke coming from the windows, police said. According to the release, both occupants were smoking marijuana and officers noticed a questionable inspection sticker. The stop took place near Delhi Street and Wooddale Avenue.

Officers asked both occupants to step out, police said. The passenger, identified as Kareem Seales, resisted and leaned back into the vehicle before officers helped him out, according to the release. During a pat-frisk, officers said they felt a hard metal object near his waistline and recovered a firearm from his front hoodie pocket.
Police said a records check showed Seales did not have a license to carry. Detectives identified the weapon as a Charter Arms revolver loaded with five rounds of .38-caliber ammunition.

Seales was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on charges of carrying a firearm without a license, carrying a loaded firearm without a license, and possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card, police said. He is presumed innocent. The release did not say whether the driver faced any charges.

sources.title: District B-3 Officers Arrest Hyde Park Man, Recover Loaded Revolver

stories.title: State Police Barracks on Martha's Vineyard Under Scrutiny After Rape Charge
stories.dek: A Boston Public Schools administrator is accused of raping a woman at the Oak Bluffs barracks, prompting a State Police internal review and a ban on overnight guests.
body: A State Police barracks in Oak Bluffs on Martha's Vineyard has become the focus of a rape investigation after prosecutors charged a Boston Public Schools administrator who had been staying there as a trooper's guest, the Boston Globe reported.

Prosecutors allege that Edward J. Brown, 27, an assistant director in the district's Office of Emergency Management, met a woman at a cafe in Oak Bluffs on Aug. 15, brought her to the barracks and raped her, according to the Globe. Brown was arraigned on a rape charge this week. He was arrested the previous Friday at Boston Latin Academy, where authorities reportedly found a powder believed to be cocaine; he faces a separate related charge. He has been placed on leave and is presumed innocent.

Brown had been a guest of trooper Ryan T. Costello, who was not present at the time, according to court records cited by the Globe. State Police opened an internal affairs investigation and declined to comment on Costello. His lawyer could not be reached.

Col. Geoffrey Noble called the allegations deeply troubling and ordered a review of policies and visitor procedures, the Globe reported. Late Friday he banned overnight guests at temporary trooper housing on Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket and required commander approval and escorts for visitors in nonpublic barracks areas. Gov. Maura Healey called the alleged crime horrific and pledged zero tolerance.
As of publication, State Police had not provided their guest policies or visitor logs to the Globe.

sources.title: 'Not here, in this quiet town': State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard becomes unlikely scene of alleged rape

stories.title: Globe Column Traces How Friends and Family Pushed for Answers in Farwell Case
stories.dek: As the federal murder trial of former Stoughton police officer Matthew Farwell continues, a Globe columnist examines how those close to the woman he is accused of killing kept her case alive.
body: A Boston Globe column published Oct. 17 looks at how relatives and friends of a Canton woman pressed authorities to reexamine her 2021 death, which is now at the center of the federal murder trial of former Stoughton police detective Matthew Farwell.

The woman, who was pregnant, was found dead in her Canton apartment in February 2021, according to the column by Yvonne Abraham. The state medical examiner and State Police initially concluded she had taken her own life. Her family later hired a forensic expert who concluded she had been killed, the Globe reported, and relatives gave State Police a broken necklace found on the bedroom floor that an expert said suggested a struggle.

According to the column, a Stoughton police internal investigation authorized by Chief Donna McNamara found that Farwell and other officers had inappropriate relationships with the woman. Federal authorities arrested Farwell in August 2024.

Prosecutors allege Farwell killed the woman to keep her from revealing abuse and staged the scene. Farwell has pleaded not guilty, and his attorneys say she took her own life after he ended their relationship. He is presumed innocent.
The trial is underway in federal court in Boston. After its first week, friends and relatives had testified about her plans for the future, according to the Globe.

sources.title: Sandra Birchmore deserved to be heard. After her death, others made sure she was.

stories.title: Olivia Rodrigo Opens Three Sold-Out Nights at TD Garden
stories.dek: Rodrigo's Unraveled Tour stop, organized around the seasons, ran about two hours on Oct. 15, according to a Boston.com review.
body: Olivia Rodrigo played the first of three sold-out shows at TD Garden on Thursday, Oct. 15, bringing her Unraveled Tour to Boston, according to a review and setlist published by Boston.com. Additional shows were scheduled for Oct. 17 and 18.

The roughly two-hour performance was structured in acts that follow the seasons, each introduced by a video and an outfit change, Boston.com reviewer Heather Alterisio wrote. The show moved from a flower-covered spring opening to a summer segment with sparklers and fire imagery, then to an autumn set on a B-stage and a winter segment staged in simulated rain on a third stage.

According to the setlist, Rodrigo opened with "drop dead" and performed songs including "good 4 u," "vampire," "traitor" and "drivers license" before an encore that closed with "expectations." The review noted that a remix of that song featuring Chappell Roan was released the same day.

Rock band Wolf Alice opened the show. The review said Rodrigo introduced each member of her band, which is made up of women and nonbinary musicians, and that light-up wristbands lit the arena during one segment.

Alterisio praised Rodrigo's shifts between quiet, intimate songs and pop-punk numbers and wrote that her confidence and stage presence showed clear growth. Photographers were not permitted at the Boston show, according to Boston.com.

sources.title: Review & setlist: Olivia Rodrigo proves music and self-worth could be 'the cure' in first of three sold-out Boston shows

stories.title: Police Seek Six People in Trespassing Case at Unfinished South Station Tower
stories.dek: Boston police released images of six young people they say climbed to the 52nd floor of the unfinished tower in September.
body: Boston police are asking for the public's help identifying six young people wanted in connection with a trespassing investigation at the unfinished South Station Tower, according to Boston.com, citing a department release.

Surveillance footage shows four people entering the parking garage at 680 Atlantic Ave. shortly after 6:30 p.m. on Sept. 7, police said. A preliminary investigation found they went through an unlocked service corridor door and climbed a stairwell to the 52nd floor.
Two more people followed the same route shortly afterward, according to police, and covered a security camera with a jacket before entering the 52nd floor.
Investigators believe the first group stayed about 45 minutes and the second about 90 minutes, police said. Both groups left through a stairwell that leads toward the Amtrak terminal level.

No arrests or charges were reported, and the people in the images were not identified. Police asked anyone with information to contact District A-1 detectives at 617-343-4571. Anonymous tips can be made by calling 1-800-494-8477 or through the department's website.

sources.title: Police want to know why these young men snuck up 52 floors in unfinished South Station Tower

stories.title: Woman Expected to Survive Dorchester Shooting, Police Say
stories.dek: Boston police said a woman was shot near 765 Washington St. on Thursday evening and no arrests have been made.
body: A woman who was shot in Dorchester on Thursday evening is expected to survive her injuries, Boston police said Friday, according to the Boston Globe.

Officers responded just before 8 p.m. Thursday to a report of a shooting near 765 Washington St. in Dorchester, police said. Police shared details about the incident on Friday, the day after the shooting, according to the Globe.

The woman was taken to a local hospital with injuries that were not believed to be life-threatening, according to police, who said she was expected to survive. Police did not release her name or her age, and did not provide additional details about her injuries.
No arrests had been made as of Friday, and the Globe's report did not mention any charges, suspects or a possible motive. Police did not describe the circumstances that led to the shooting.
Boston police said the investigation is ongoing. The Globe's brief report, published in its Crime and Courts section, did not include further details from authorities.

sources.title: Woman expected to survive shooting in Dorchester, police say

stories.title: Healey Criticized Over Debate Response to Vineyard Barracks Rape Case
stories.dek: Victim advocates and her Republican challenger faulted Gov. Maura Healey's debate remarks about a rape allegation at a State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard.
body: Gov. Maura Healey drew criticism after saying during a Thursday night debate that sometimes things happen when asked about misconduct in the State Police, following a rape allegation at the agency's Martha's Vineyard barracks, the Boston Globe reported.

During the Oct. 15 debate with Republican challenger Michael Minogue, Healey said she and State Police Col. Geoffrey D. Noble make sure swift action is taken, and said she is proud of the State Police and that Noble is doing a good job, according to the Globe.

The case involves Edward J. Brown, 27, a Boston Public Schools security official who was arrested Oct. 9 at Boston Latin Academy. He is charged with raping a woman he brought to the barracks, where he was staying as a trooper's guest. Brown pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Edgartown District Court, the Globe reported, and is presumed innocent.

Amanda Walsh of the Victim Rights Law Center told the Globe the governor missed a chance to reassure survivors. Minogue called the response unacceptable. Healey noted that Brown is a civilian, not a State Police member, and in a separate statement called the alleged assault a horrific crime and said there is zero tolerance for such conduct.
State Police opened an internal affairs investigation, and Noble barred overnight guests at temporary trooper housing on Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket, according to the Globe.

sources.title: 'It feels like a miss.' Healey draws criticism for 'things happen' response in Vineyard barracks rape case.

stories.title: Southbridge Man Charged With Assault in Case Tied to Fatal Worcester Shooting
stories.dek: Prosecutors say the man struck a victim with an object resembling a handgun minutes before that man was fatally shot near a Worcester club; he has not been charged in the shooting.
body: A Southbridge man has been arrested in connection with an Oct. 11 shooting near Hurricane Betty's strip club in Worcester that killed one man and critically injured another, the Boston Globe reported.

Jose I. Hiciano, 23, was arraigned Thursday in Worcester District Court on a charge of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, according to the Worcester District Attorney's office. A police report alleges he repeatedly struck a man in the head with an object resembling a handgun on a sidewalk near the club minutes before that man was fatally shot, the Globe reported.

Police said surveillance video recorded the alleged assault at 2:04 a.m., and two gunshots were recorded about two minutes later. A spokesperson for the district attorney said no additional charges related to the shooting had been filed. Authorities have not said who fired the shots.

Bail was set at $100,000, and Hiciano was taken to the Worcester County Jail after he did not post it, according to the Globe. His attorney, Blake J. Rubin, said the bail was too high for the charge and argued prosecutors had offered no real evidence linking his client to the shooting. Hiciano is presumed innocent.
A hearing to contest the bail was expected Tuesday, and a pretrial hearing is scheduled for Nov. 13. The wounded man's condition was not available as of Friday.

sources.title: Southbridge man arrested in connection with shooting near Worcester strip club

stories.title: Man Killed After Being Ejected From Vehicle in Sharon Crash
stories.dek: Police said the man's vehicle struck a guardrail on Old Post Road Thursday night; local and state authorities are investigating.
body: A man died after he was ejected from his vehicle in a crash in Sharon on Thursday night, police said, according to the Boston Globe.

Police responded around 10 p.m. to a reported crash in the area of Old Post Road near South Main Street, the Globe reported. According to police, the vehicle struck a guardrail and the man was thrown from it.
Police have not released the man's name. The Globe's report did not say whether anyone else was in the vehicle or whether the man died at the scene or later at a hospital.

Local police, State Police and the Norfolk District Attorney's Office are investigating the crash, according to the Globe. Authorities had not released information about what may have caused the vehicle to leave the road and hit the guardrail.
No charges were mentioned in the report. The investigation remains ongoing, and officials had not provided additional details as of the Globe's report.

sources.title: Man killed after being ejected from vehicle in Sharon crash

stories.title: Police Seek Two People After Tip Jar Theft at Jamaica Plain Restaurant
stories.dek: Boston police released images of a man and a woman they want to identify in a larceny at a Washington Street restaurant.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify a man and a woman in connection with a larceny at a restaurant on Washington Street in Jamaica Plain, according to a department community alert.

Officers from District E-13 responded at about 5:42 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 9, to a report of a larceny at the restaurant at 3160 Washington St., police said. According to the victim, the theft happened at about 7:40 p.m. the previous evening, Oct. 8.
The victim told police that an unknown man and woman came into the restaurant and bought food, then took a tip jar along with straws and napkins, according to the alert.
Police released two images in connection with the investigation. No arrests or charges were announced, and the alert did not include physical descriptions of the two people.

District E-13 detectives are investigating. Anyone with information is asked to call detectives at 617-343-5628. Anonymous tips can be made through CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting TIP to 27463, or online through the Boston Police Department's website.

sources.title: BPD Community Alert: Detectives Seek Public's Assistance in Efforts to Identify Two Individuals in Relation to a Larceny Investigation in Jamaica Plain

stories.title: Fiddlehead, Couch and Ripe Lead 2026 Boston Music Awards Nominations
stories.dek: The awards, which add a classical category this year, return to Big Night Live on Dec. 16, with public voting open through Nov. 16.
body: The Boston Music Awards announced its 2026 nominees on Friday and opened public voting, with Fiddlehead, Couch and Ripe each receiving six nominations, the Boston Globe reported.
The ceremony returns to Big Night Live on Dec. 16 and will name winners in 52 categories, according to the Globe. The awards were launched in 1987.
Artist of the Year nominees are Bebe Stockwell, Clark D, Converge, Couch, Fiddlehead, Haywire, Ripe, The Elovaters, Tiny Habits and Token, according to the list.

This year adds a Classical Artist/Ensemble of the Year category. Its nominees include the Boston Symphony Orchestra, the Boston Pops, Boston Baroque, the Handel and Haydn Society, A Far Cry, Castle of Our Skins and Yo-Yo Ma, the Globe reported. Other categories cover new artists, albums, songs, videos, genres, venues, promoters, studios and media.

Paul Armstrong, chief executive of Redefined and producer of the awards, told the Globe the ballot showed a local scene with continued energy, pointing to Boston artists who have toured widely and appeared on national television.
Voting is open through 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 16 at bostonmusicawards.com, where tickets are also on sale.

sources.title: See the full list of nominees for the 2026 Boston Music Awards

stories.title: New Openings Include Cambridge Robata Bar, Second Michette Bakery
stories.dek: Boston.com's weekly dining roundup lists openings in Cambridge, Braintree and downtown, plus a poutine festival in the Seaport.
body: A Japanese charcoal-grill bar, a second location of a French bakery and an expanding ramen chain are among the latest dining openings in the Boston area, according to Boston.com's weekly roundup by Nathan Tavares.

EnYa Robatayaki & Sake Bar is coming to 125 River St. in Cambridge, the former What A Soup space, with skewers grilled over charcoal and sake in an izakaya-style setting, Boston.com reported. It is expected to open this fall, with details to come on Instagram.
Michette Bakery has opened a second location at 305 Webster Ave. in Inman Square, serving croissants, pastries, breads and savory items, along with coffee and drinks, according to the roundup.

Ramen Haven, a local chain that started in Berlin, Massachusetts, is opening at the South Shore Mall in Braintree in October and at 832 Commonwealth Ave. in December, Boston.com reported. The Sports Bra, a bar that shows only women's sports, is planning to open at 2 Broad St. downtown by year's end.
The roundup also noted PoutineFest at Harpoon, 306 Northern Ave. in the Seaport, on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 11:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., with tickets starting at $54.99.

sources.title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (October 16, 2026)

stories.title: Judge Revokes Bail for Former Healey Aide LaMar Cook After Federal Fraud Charges
stories.dek: A Hampden County judge sent Cook back to jail for 90 days a day after federal prosecutors charged him with SNAP and wire fraud.
body: LaMar D. Cook, a former aide to Gov. Maura Healey who already faces gun and drug trafficking charges, was ordered back to jail Thursday after federal prosecutors charged him with fraud, the Boston Globe reported.

Hampden County Judge David Hodge granted a motion by state prosecutors to revoke Cook's bail in his state case and ordered him held for 90 days, according to the Globe. Prosecutors argued there was probable cause he had violated federal law and that he was unlikely to follow release conditions.

On Wednesday, the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts charged Cook, 46, of Springfield, with SNAP fraud and wire fraud. Federal prosecutors allege he received nearly $550 a month in food assistance by falsely claiming he had no income and less than $100 in the bank, while his balance was about $13,000 in January, the Globe reported. He was released after a federal hearing Wednesday.

Cook was arrested in October 2025 after police allegedly seized about 17 pounds of cocaine set to be delivered to the Springfield state building where he worked for Healey. He was released on $25,000 bail in March.

His lawyer, Kedar Ismail, said he respects the judge's decision and looks forward to clearing Cook's name, and argued in court the motion was political. U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley criticized the state's oversight. Healey, who appointed Cook in 2023, said it was good he had been charged, according to the Globe. Cook is presumed innocent.

sources.title: LaMar Cook, former Healey aide facing drug trafficking case, sent back to jail in wake of federal SNAP fraud charges

stories.title: Boston to Launch Five Free City-Run Shuttle Routes in Early 2027
stories.dek: Mayor Michelle Wu's Link Bus Program, funded by an $11.5 million federal grant, will connect neighborhoods to transit stops for three years.
body: Boston plans to launch five free shuttle bus routes to connect residential neighborhoods with public transit, Mayor Michelle Wu's administration announced, according to Boston.com.

The Link Bus Program will serve Mattapan, Roxbury, Allston-Brighton, Charlestown and the Lower Mystic, and the Seaport, the city said. The routes are meant to close so-called first-mile and last-mile gaps between where riders start or end their trips and the transit system.

The shuttles will run for three years with $11.5 million from the Federal Highway Administration's Congestion Relief Program, according to the city. The Economic Development and Industrial Corporation of Boston voted to accept the funding at its Sept. 17 meeting. Service is expected to begin in early 2027, with schedules and route information posted on the city's website at launch.

The Allston-Brighton, Charlestown and Lower Mystic, and Seaport services will be run with existing local transportation organizations, Boston.com reported. Routes in Mattapan and Roxbury have not been finalized; the city is working with residents on destinations and will choose operators through competitive procurement.

Wu said the program would bring free transportation into neighborhoods and strengthen connections to the MBTA. The city said it will look for ways to sustain the service after the three-year grant period.

sources.title: Wu's new plan to expand free public transit: free city-run shuttles

stories.title: Jury Orders Boston Water and Sewer Commission to Pay $1 Million for Retaliation
stories.dek: A Suffolk County jury rejected a former manager's discrimination claims but found the commission retaliated against him after he sued; the commission plans to appeal.
body: A Suffolk County jury on Thursday ordered the Boston Water and Sewer Commission to pay $1 million to a former employee, finding the agency retaliated against him after he sued over alleged racial discrimination, the Boston Globe reported.

The jury rejected the discrimination claims brought by Terrance Williams, a Black Dorchester resident who joined the commission in 1988 and became manager of operations in 2017, according to the Globe. The award includes $400,000 in punitive damages, his attorney said.

Williams sued in 2022, alleging the commission underpaid and passed over Black employees, including himself, in favor of less experienced white colleagues. He said that after he filed suit he was reprimanded over a parking spot, had performance reviews altered and was denied promotion interviews. He was fired in May 2025.

His attorney, Nick Carter, told the Globe the commission fired Williams for standing up for Black workers and urged city and state leaders to scrutinize the agency. Commission attorney Brian T. Kelly said the agency was pleased the jury rejected the discrimination claims and will appeal the retaliation finding. Kelly said Williams was fired for working a second job with the sheriff's department while on the clock.
The commission serves more than a million people daily and employs about 450 people, according to the Globe.

sources.title: Jury verdict: Boston Water and Sewer Commission must pay $1 million for retaliation against former employee

stories.title: Jacob Collier to Give First Performance at Museum of Science's New Venue
stories.dek: The English musician was set to open the museum's 500-person Bloomberg Public Science Common on Oct. 16, according to the Boston Globe.
body: English multi-instrumentalist and composer Jacob Collier was scheduled to give the first performance at the Museum of Science's newest space on Friday, Oct. 16, the Boston Globe reported in its weekly music column.

The William and Charlotte Bloomberg Public Science Common is a 500-person, 10,000-square-foot multipurpose venue with rotating LED boards and an ambient sound system of 46 individually programmable speakers, according to the Globe.

Collier's show was designed around those features, the Globe reported. He has described Boston as a second home; his local ties include an honorary doctorate and commencement address at Berklee in May 2026, performances with the Boston Pops and a residency at MIT.

Museum president Tim Ritchie told the Globe that Collier has a rare ability to create wonder and that he hopes other performing artists will make use of the space's technology. He said the musician's connections to MIT and technology made him a fitting choice for the launch.

Other upcoming programs in the space include talks by Zakim Bridge architect Miguel Rosales, conservationist Paul Rosolie and former NASA engineer Mark Rober, according to the Globe. Vivo Performing Arts has booked February shows featuring choreographer Huang Yi performing with an industrial robot arm.

sources.title: Jacob Collier has left his mark on Berklee, Symphony Hall, and MIT. Now he's coming to the Museum of Science.

stories.title: Boston Schools Employee Pleads Not Guilty to Rape Charge in Oak Bluffs Case
stories.dek: Prosecutors allege a Boston Public Schools security employee assaulted a woman at the State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard this summer.
body: A Boston Public Schools security employee pleaded not guilty Tuesday in Edgartown District Court to raping a woman at the State Police barracks in Oak Bluffs on Martha's Vineyard this summer, according to Boston.com.

Edward Joseph Brown, 27, of Boston, was arrested Oct. 9 at Boston Latin Academy by Oak Bluffs and Boston police, Boston.com reported. Prosecutors said police found suspected cocaine in his wallet at the time of the arrest.

According to prosecutors, the woman told police she met a man at a bar who bought her a drink and that she later woke up in an unfamiliar place with him. Prosecutors said cellphone data tracked a rideshare trip to the barracks. A state trooper told investigators Brown had been visiting him on the island that week, according to Boston.com.

Brown is being held at the Dukes County jail on $10,000 cash bail and is due back in court Dec. 3. His lawyer, Anthony Ellison, said Brown maintains his innocence and looks forward to trial. He is presumed innocent.

Boston Public Schools placed Brown on administrative leave and said the charges do not involve students. Oak Bluffs police said the arrest followed an independent investigation with the Cape and Islands District Attorney's Office, and that the case remains under investigation. State Police have opened an internal probe.

sources.title: Boston Public Schools employee charged with raping woman at State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard

stories.title: Dorchester Man Arrested on Gun Charges After Foot Chase in Mattapan
stories.dek: Boston police said officers recovered a loaded pistol along the man's path after a group ran from an altercation near Mallard Avenue.
body: Boston police arrested a 22-year-old Dorchester man on multiple firearm charges Tuesday night after a foot chase in Mattapan, according to a department release.

Officers from District B-3 on directed patrol at about 10:50 p.m. on Oct. 13 saw an altercation in the street near Talbot Avenue and Mallard Avenue, where several people were gathered around an idling vehicle outside 16 Mallard Ave., police said. According to the release, officers saw one man pull an item from under his hoodie near his left armpit and a second man appear to press an object against his midsection.

The group ran when they noticed officers, police said. Officers caught Corey Perfect Jean-Little, who was not wearing shoes, behind 86 Southern Ave. The second man and the vehicle left the area, according to the release.

Officers searching the route he ran found a firearm, a pair of shoes and a cellphone in the driveway of 16 Mallard Ave., police said. Detectives identified the gun as a Taurus Millennium with a light attachment, loaded with one round in the chamber and two in a 30-round-capacity magazine.

Jean-Little was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on charges including carrying a firearm without a license, second offense; possession of a large-capacity firearm; possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card; and trespassing, police said. He is presumed innocent. The release did not say whether the second man had been identified.

sources.title: Mattapan Officers Recovered a Firearm Following a Foot Chase

stories.title: One Killed, One Wounded in Double Shooting Outside Worcester Club
stories.dek: Worcester police said two people were found shot early Sunday at the address of the Hurricane Betty's club on Southbridge Street.
body: One person was killed and another was wounded in a double shooting in Worcester early Sunday, according to Worcester police, as reported by Boston.com.
Police responded at about 2 a.m. to two ShotSpotter gunshot-detection activations at 350 Southbridge St., the address of the adult entertainment club Hurricane Betty's, Boston.com reported.

Officers found two males with gunshot wounds, police said. Both were taken to a nearby hospital in critical condition, and one of them later died, according to the department, which described the shooting in a Facebook post on Tuesday.

No suspects had been named and no arrests or charges were reported as of Boston.com's report. An employee at the club declined to comment when reached by phone, and the Worcester County District Attorney's Office said no further information was available Wednesday night.
Worcester police and the Worcester County District Attorney's Office are continuing to investigate the shooting. Authorities had not released the names or ages of the two people who were shot.

sources.title: 1 killed in double shooting in Worcester

stories.title: Two Teens Charged in Dorchester Liquor Store Robbery, DA Says
stories.dek: Suffolk County prosecutors charged a 14-year-old and a 15-year-old with armed robbery after a confrontation at a Dorchester Avenue store on Oct. 1.
body: Two juveniles were charged last week in Dorchester Juvenile Court in connection with a theft and assault at a liquor store on Dorchester Avenue, the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office said in a press release.

Boston police responded at about 11 a.m. on Oct. 1 to a reported fight at the store, according to the release. The owner told police a group of juveniles came in, took four packs of canned drinks and assaulted him and his wife.

According to prosecutors, surveillance video shows one unidentified juvenile putting the drinks in a backpack and leaving while a 15-year-old went behind the counter. Prosecutors allege that as the group ran out, the 15-year-old pinned a worker against a wall and a 14-year-old struck the worker on the head with a bag holding two unopened cans. Transit police held the group until Boston police arrived; they were given a trespass warning and released, and arrest warrants were later issued, the DA's office said.

The 15-year-old is charged with armed robbery. The 14-year-old is charged with armed robbery and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon. Both were released on personal recognizance and ordered to stay away from the victim and the store. They are presumed innocent.
District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the alleged conduct was troubling and that his office uses youth programs when appropriate.

sources.title: Two juveniles charged with stealing from liquor store, one charged with assaulting worker

stories.title: Elderly Couple Found Dead in Attleboro Home After Fire
stories.dek: Responders conducting a wellness check found the couple on Andover Avenue; officials said the fire was not considered suspicious.
body: A married couple, ages 78 and 76, were found dead inside their Andover Avenue home in Attleboro on Wednesday after a fire, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

Emergency responders found the couple just before 11:30 a.m. on Oct. 14 while conducting a wellness check, the Globe reported. After they were unable to reach anyone inside, responders forced their way into the house and found a fire still smoldering on the first floor, which firefighters put out.
Officials said responders found evidence of a significant fire inside the house, according to the Globe. The report did not say how long the fire had been burning before the couple were found.
Investigators determined the fire was not suspicious, officials said. The couple were formally identified by authorities on Thursday, the day after they were found.
The causes of the fire and of the deaths remain under investigation, the Globe reported. The report did not specify which agencies were leading the investigation.

sources.title: Elderly couple found dead in Attleboro home after fire, officials say

stories.title: Boston Book Festival and Fort Point Open Studios Headline Weekend Events
stories.dek: WBUR's weekend guide for Oct. 15-18 included dance premieres, free events in Copley Square and City Hall Plaza, and a concert of spirituals in Roxbury.
body: The Boston Book Festival and Fort Point Open Studios were among the events highlighted in WBUR's guide to the weekend of Oct. 15 to 18.

The book festival held a free day of programming in Copley Square on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., featuring a panel with authors Dawn Tripp, Laura Zigman and Alice Hoffman, a storytime session with Edwidge Danticat and a reading by Boston Poet Laureate Emmanuel Oppong-Yeboah, according to WBUR. A ticketed Friday event at Old South Church paired Michael Lewis and Geraldine Brooks.

Fort Point Open Studios ran Friday evening and from noon to 6 p.m. Saturday and Sunday at sites including the Eli Lilly Building and Midway Artist Studios, WBUR reported. The free event also included Boston Lyric Opera rehearsal viewings and a Boston Children's Museum art lab.

Boston Conservatory at Berklee presented From the Ground Up, six world premieres by guest and faculty choreographers, with tickets starting at $43.50. On City Hall Plaza, the free Sweater Weather Fest offered talks, film screenings and DJ sets on Saturday.

Castle of Our Skins, presented by Vivo Performing Arts, performed Sacred Transcendence, a free program of African American spirituals, at Twelfth Baptist Church in Roxbury on Saturday afternoon, according to WBUR.

sources.title: 5 things to do this weekend, including Fort Point Open Studios and Boston Book Festival

stories.title: Cambridge Man Arrested After Alleged Assaults in South End's Blackstone Square
stories.dek: Boston police said a man assaulted and threatened people in the park and punched an officer before being taken into custody; two officers were hospitalized.
body: Boston police arrested a 26-year-old Cambridge man Monday evening after they say he assaulted several people in Blackstone Square in the South End and fought with officers, according to a department release.

Officers from District D-4 responded at about 5:34 p.m. on Oct. 12 to a report of an assault and battery in progress at the park, at 1535 Washington St., police said. Witnesses pointed out the man, who walked away and ignored commands, according to the release.

When a second officer arrived, police said, the man took a fighting stance outside 35 W. Newton St., tried to enter the building and punched an officer in the face. An officer used a Taser, and a struggle followed before additional officers and civilians helped take him into custody.

According to police, the man knocked a cellphone from one person's hand and took it; officers later returned it. Police allege he grabbed another man's wrist, demanded his watch, then shoved him to the ground and punched him. A woman walking in the park told police he threatened to kill her.

Two officers were taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said. Sharkell Tariq Matthews was expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court on charges including assault with intent to rob, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, assault and battery on an elderly person and resisting arrest. He is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Violent Suspect Arrested After Assaulting Multiple Victims and Officers in Blackstone Square

stories.title: Man Charged With Trying to Disarm Officer During South End Arrest
stories.dek: Boston police said a 34-year-old man grabbed at an officer's Taser and gun as a struggle moved into a rain-soaked Massachusetts Avenue.
body: Boston police arrested a 34-year-old man Sunday in the South End after he allegedly tried to take an officer's firearm during a struggle, according to Boston.com, citing a department release.

Officers were called shortly after 7 p.m. to a report of a group using drugs at the entrance of a private residence near 690 Massachusetts Ave., police said. Officers recognized Felix Omar David Marrero from a previous encounter, according to police. They said he gave a false name, but officers confirmed his identity and found two outstanding warrants on drug charges.

When officers tried to arrest him, police said, Marrero locked his hands together to avoid being handcuffed, ignored commands and fought with officers. According to the release, the struggle moved into the street amid heavy rain and traffic.
Police allege Marrero tried and failed to grab an officer's Taser, then grabbed the handle of an officer's firearm before officers pried his hand away. Additional units helped take him into custody.

He was charged with attempted assault and battery to disarm a police officer, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, resisting arrest, disorderly conduct, disturbing the peace and receiving stolen property, Boston.com reported. No court dates were reported. He is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Man charged after allegedly trying to disarm officer during violent street arrest

stories.title: Two Sentenced to Prison for 2023 Fatal Stabbing Near Mass. and Cass
stories.dek: Both defendants pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the death of a 39-year-old woman on Topeka Street, the Suffolk District Attorney's office said.
body: Two Boston residents have been sentenced to state prison after pleading guilty to manslaughter in the 2023 fatal stabbing of a woman near Massachusetts Avenue and Melnea Cass Boulevard, the Boston Globe reported, citing the Suffolk District Attorney's office.

Michael Bellanti, 35, was sentenced Tuesday to 10 to 15 years in prison, according to the Globe. Crystal Morgan, 41, was scheduled to begin jury selection Wednesday in Suffolk Superior Court but instead pleaded guilty and was sentenced to six to eight years, the DA's office said.

According to prosecutors, the attack happened on the evening of Aug. 18, 2023, on Topeka Street, after Boston police broke up a fight on nearby Atkinson Street. Prosecutors said Bellanti approached the 39-year-old woman and stabbed her while Morgan held her arm and kept her from leaving. The woman was taken to a hospital, where she died.
Morgan had pleaded not guilty to second-degree murder at her 2023 arraignment, according to court records cited by the Globe.

A statement from a friend of the woman was read in court describing her as more than the circumstances of her death. District Attorney Kevin R. Hayden said the friend's words carried an important message about her life.

sources.title: Two sentenced to prison for 2023 fatal stabbing of woman near Mass. and Cass, officials say

stories.title: Chelsea Building Declared Structurally Unsafe After Partial Collapse
stories.dek: Nine residents were displaced after part of the front facade of a century-old brick building on Orange Street fell Sunday night, city officials said.
body: Nine residents were displaced after the front facade of a three-story brick building on Orange Street in Chelsea partially collapsed Sunday night, city officials said, according to the Boston Globe. No injuries were reported.

Firefighters responded at about 8 p.m. to 38-40 Orange St. and found major structural damage to the second and third floors of the facade and a large amount of brick and concrete debris on the sidewalk, officials said. Residents were moved out as a precaution, and the owner and fire department helped relocate them.

A drone inspection later found a separation between the front and side walls, a sagging roof and a lean in the building, according to the city. A Monday inspection found both 38 and 40 Orange St. unsafe for occupancy, and the fire alarm system was also affected.

Mike McAteer, Chelsea's director of inspectional services, said the building dates to around 1890 to 1900 and attributed the collapse to water entering cracks in the brick, freezing and gradually fracturing the wall over roughly a century, the Globe reported.

Firefighters remained at the scene because of the building's instability. The property management company's engineers were expected to assess it Tuesday, and the city said it wants to help the owner make repairs so residents can return.

sources.title: Chelsea residence deemed 'structurally unsafe' after partial collapse displaced residents, officials say

stories.title: Worcester Man Identified as Driver Killed in Arborway Crash
stories.dek: The Suffolk District Attorney's Office said a 48-year-old Worcester man died when his car was struck in a multi-vehicle crash in Jamaica Plain.
body: Authorities have identified the man killed in a multi-vehicle crash on the Arborway in Jamaica Plain on Sunday as a 48-year-old Worcester resident, according to Boston.com.
The man was driving a car that was struck by another vehicle shortly after 2 p.m., according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Dashcam footage obtained by WHDH shows a white sedan going over a concrete median and colliding with a red SUV traveling in the opposite direction, Boston.com reported. WHDH reported that the sedan's 18-year-old driver was allegedly speeding and lost control.
Another man was injured and remains hospitalized, according to the report. The DA's office has not publicly identified him, and prosecutors have not said whether he will face criminal charges.
Massachusetts State Police and the Suffolk District Attorney's Office are continuing to investigate the crash, which earlier reports said was the subject of a criminal investigation.

sources.title: Victim in fatal Jamaica Plain Arborway crash identified

stories.title: Women's Sports Bar The Sports Bra Prepares to Open Downtown
stories.dek: A group of eight Boston locals is finishing renovations on a Broad Street space for the franchise, which shows only women's sports.
body: The Sports Bra, a sports bar that shows only women's sports, is preparing to open its Boston location at 2 Broad St. in the Financial District, according to Boston.com.
The 3,243-square-foot space previously housed Tiki Rock, Boston.com reported. No opening date has been announced, though a sign on the door reads "Game time: Fall 2026."

The bar will have a large seating area and TVs showing local and national women's games, including Boston Legacy FC of the NWSL, the Boston Fleet of the PWHL and the Boston Hunters of the WPBL, according to the report. The owners said it will be family-friendly and will prioritize sourcing from local, women-owned businesses.

The franchise is owned by eight Boston friends whose idea started in a group chat, Boston.com reported. In 2024 they launched Watch With Us Boston, which hosted pop-up watch parties, and in early 2025 they signed a franchise agreement. Owner Lydia Coverdale-Perez said the group saw the space as the right fit, and spokesperson Dana Marie Cincis described the venue as a community hub for women's sports.

The original Sports Bra opened in Portland, Oregon, in 2022. Founder Jenny Nguyen announced expansion in 2025 to Boston and Portland, Maine, and praised the Boston ownership group's leadership, according to Boston.com.

sources.title: A women's sports bar, The Sports Bra Boston, is preparing for its opening day downtown

stories.title: The Sports Bra Franchise Announces Financial District Location
stories.dek: The women's sports bar chain, founded in Portland, Oregon, will open in the former Tiki Rock space on Broad Street, the Boston Globe reported.
body: The Sports Bra, a franchise billed as the first sports bar dedicated exclusively to women's sports, has announced a Boston location at 2 Broad St. in the Financial District, the Boston Globe reported.
Renovations at the 3,243-square-foot former Tiki Rock space are nearly complete, according to the Globe, but an opening date has not been set. A sign on the door reads "Game time: Fall 2026."

The bar will feature a large bar area and TVs showing local and national women's sports, including the Boston Legacy, the Boston Fleet and the Boston Hunters, the Globe reported. It is planned as a family-friendly venue with a broad food and drink menu and an emphasis on products from local, women-owned businesses.

The Boston franchise is owned by a group of eight Boston-area friends who formed Watch With Us Boston in 2024 to host pop-up watch parties, according to the Globe. Growing crowds led them to seek a permanent venue, and they signed with The Sports Bra in early 2025. Spokesperson Dana Marie Cincis said the goal is a community hub for women's sports history, education and visibility.
The first Sports Bra opened in Portland, Oregon, in 2022. Founder Jenny Nguyen announced franchise expansion in 2025, including Boston and Portland, Maine.

sources.title: Women's sports bar franchise The Sports Bra announces Boston location

stories.title: One Dead, One Critically Injured in Shooting Near Worcester Club
stories.dek: Worcester police said two men were shot early Sunday after ShotSpotter detected gunfire on Southbridge Street.
body: One man was killed and another was critically injured in a shooting near an adult entertainment club in Worcester early Sunday, police said, according to the Boston Globe.
Officers responded just after 2 a.m. to two ShotSpotter activations for gunshots at 350 Southbridge St., the address of the club Hurricane Betty's, the Globe reported.

Both men were taken to a nearby hospital for treatment, according to police. One of them later died of his injuries, and the other was described as critically injured. Police did not release the names or ages of either man.
The Globe's report did not include information about any arrests, suspects or a possible motive in the shooting, and police did not say whether anyone else was involved.

Police had not described the circumstances that led to the shooting. The Globe's report, filed in its Crime and Courts section on Oct. 13, said no further information was immediately available at the time of publication.

sources.title: One man dead, one injured after shooting near Worcester strip club, police say

stories.title: Police Identify Man Killed in Whitfield Street Shooting in Dorchester
stories.dek: Boston police said a 21-year-old Dorchester man died after a Sept. 30 shooting, and a 20-year-old has been arraigned on a murder charge.
body: Boston police have identified the man fatally shot on Whitfield Street in Dorchester last month as a 21-year-old Dorchester resident, according to a department update.

Officers from District B-2 responded at about 5:39 p.m. on Wednesday, Sept. 30, to a report of a person shot in the area of 7 Whitfield St., police said. They found the man with an apparent gunshot wound and took him to a local hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.
Detectives identified Joseph Bailey, 20, of Dorchester, as a suspect, according to the department. Bailey was arraigned in Dorchester District Court on a murder charge. He is presumed innocent.

The department's Homicide Unit is continuing to review the case, police said. Anyone with information is asked to call homicide detectives at 617-343-4470. Anonymous tips can be made through CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting TIP to 27463.
The Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers free, confidential support around the clock at 617-431-0125, according to the department.

sources.title: Investigation Update: Victim Identified in 7 Whitfield Street Homicide

stories.title: Man Dies After Contact With Red Line Third Rail Near Neponset River Bridge
stories.dek: MBTA Transit Police said a man trespassing on the tracks Sunday night was pronounced dead and foul play is not suspected.
body: A man died after coming into contact with the electrified third rail on the MBTA Red Line on Sunday night, MBTA Transit Police said, according to Boston.com.

The man was trespassing near the Neponset River Bridge when he touched the third rail shortly before midnight, according to Transit Police. He was pronounced dead. Police did not release his identity.

In a statement, Transit Police offered condolences to the man's family and friends, Boston.com reported. The investigation is ongoing, but officials said they do not suspect foul play. The report did not describe any effect on Red Line service.

Boston.com noted that the death follows an Aug. 30 incident in which a 19-year-old died after falling onto the third rail at Forest Hills station while he was trying to help another person, the outlet reported.
The MBTA is evaluating whether to install protective barriers along the platform edges at certain stations, according to Boston.com's report.

sources.title: Man dies after coming into contact with third rail on Red Line

stories.title: Driver Killed in Jamaica Plain Crash; Criminal Investigation Underway
stories.dek: A spokesperson for the Suffolk District Attorney's Office said one driver died and another was injured in a multi-car crash Sunday.
body: One driver was killed and another was injured in a multi-car crash in Jamaica Plain on Sunday, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, the Boston Globe reported.
James Borghesani, a spokesperson for the district attorney's office, said a criminal investigation is being conducted into the crash, according to the Globe. Police are also investigating.
Officials did not release the names of the drivers involved, and they did not provide details about what caused the crash or the condition of the injured driver, the Globe reported.
The Globe did not report the exact location of the crash within Jamaica Plain or how many vehicles were involved beyond describing it as a multi-car collision. No arrests or charges were mentioned.

No further information was immediately available from authorities, according to the Globe's report, which was published Sunday as a breaking news item in its Crime and Courts section. The investigation remains ongoing, and officials had not said when more details would be released.

sources.title: Criminal investigation underway after driver killed in Jamaica Plain crash

stories.title: Teddy Swims Plays 25-Song Set at TD Garden, Previews New Album
stories.dek: Swims debuted two unreleased songs ahead of his January album during a two-hour-plus show on Oct. 9, according to a Boston.com review.
body: Teddy Swims performed at TD Garden on Friday, Oct. 9, playing a 25-song set that ran more than two hours, according to a review and setlist published by Boston.com.

Swims took the stage at 9 p.m., descending on a platform for the opener "The Door," Boston.com reviewer Samantha Genzer wrote. He played two unreleased songs ahead of his album UGLY, due Jan. 22, along with songs including "Bad Dreams," "911" and "Devil in a Dress" and a cover of Kris Kross's "Jump." Two songs chosen by fans through pre-show voting were performed in an acoustic segment.

The production featured fireworks, a mock van crash at the back of the stage and a cannon that launched hot dogs into the crowd, according to the review. The multilevel set was modeled on Atlanta's punk and rock scene.
St. Paul and the Broken Bones, an eight-piece Alabama soul band led by Paul Janeway, played an almost hourlong opening set, preceded by producer and songwriter MarcLo, Boston.com reported.
Genzer wrote that Swims' voice and stage presence were the show's strongest elements, while noting that pacing slowed during a run of ballads and that the full evening lasted more than four hours.

sources.title: Review & setlist: Teddy Swims brings the soul — and flying hot dogs — to TD Garden

stories.title: The Chicks Mark 20 Years of 'Taking the Long Way' at MGM Music Hall
stories.dek: The trio played the 2006 album in full, paired with documentary-style video, before a second set of hits, according to a Boston.com review.
body: The Chicks performed at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on Friday, Oct. 9, on their Taking the Long Way 20th Anniversary Tour, according to a review published by Boston.com.

The nearly two-hour show had no opening act and combined music with what reviewer Chris Stevens described as a live documentary of the band's story, using video clips, home movies and personal reflections, Boston.com reported.

The first set featured all 14 tracks of the 2006 album, opening with "The Long Way Around" and including "Not Ready to Make Nice," "Easy Silence" and "Lubbock or Leave It," according to the review. Videos revisited the backlash the band faced after a 2003 comment about then-President George W. Bush and featured collaborators including John Mayer and Mike Campbell. The set closed with "I Hope."
After a short break, the band returned with hits and covers including "Goodbye Earl," "Wide Open Spaces," "Landslide" and "Sin Wagon," Boston.com reported.
Stevens gave the show a strongly positive review, praising the trio's storytelling and musicianship and describing the evening as emotionally varied.

sources.title: Review & Setlist: The Chicks bring fiery journey to stage

stories.title: 18-Year-Old Charged With Murder in Hyde Park Gas Station Shooting
stories.dek: The Suffolk District Attorney's Office said the Boston man surrendered two days after a 20-year-old was fatally shot on Hyde Park Avenue.
body: An 18-year-old Boston man turned himself in to police Friday morning and pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder in the fatal shooting of a 20-year-old man at a Hyde Park gas station, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, as reported by Boston.com.

Police allege Christian Peebles shot the man inside a gas station at 1171 Hyde Park Ave. shortly after 5 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 7, Boston.com reported. The man was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Authorities have released few details about the circumstances.

Peebles was arraigned in the West Roxbury Division of Boston Municipal Court on the murder charge and several firearms offenses and was ordered held without bail, according to the report. Judge John Garland also revoked his bail in an earlier case. He is due back in court Nov. 9 and is presumed innocent.

His attorney, Jennifer O'Brien, said Peebles turned himself in once he learned police were looking for him and that his parents brought him to the police station. She declined to comment further, citing the pending investigation.
The Boston Police Homicide Unit is investigating. Anyone with information can call 617-343-4470 or CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS.

sources.title: DA: Boston teen turned himself in after fatal Hyde Park shooting

stories.title: Brighton Man Arrested With Machete Also Charged in Triple Stabbing
stories.dek: Boston police said detectives linked the 24-year-old to an Oct. 4 stabbing near Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue that injured three men.
body: A Brighton man arrested Thursday while allegedly carrying a machete has also been charged in a triple stabbing in Brighton last weekend, according to Boston police, as reported by Boston.com.

Officers responded shortly before 5 p.m. Thursday to a report of a person swinging a large knife near Leo M. Birmingham Parkway, police said. According to police, officers found Joshua Flores, 24, walking down Western Avenue with a machete, which he dropped when told to. Officers also found a folding knife in his pocket. He was initially charged with carrying a dangerous weapon and disturbing the peace.

Police said that after further investigation, detectives developed probable cause to charge Flores in a stabbing at about 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, Oct. 4, near Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue. Officers at that scene found three men with stab wounds, and Boston EMS took them to hospitals with injuries not considered life-threatening.

Flores is charged with three counts of armed assault with intent to murder, three counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and two counts of mayhem, Boston.com reported.
Judge Shelley Joseph ordered him held without bail pending a dangerousness hearing on Oct. 15. It was not immediately clear whether he had an attorney. He is presumed innocent.

stories.title: Two Men Wanted in Stabbing of NYPD Detective Arrested in Lynn
stories.dek: U.S. Marshals said a multi-agency team took the men into custody Tuesday night; they await extradition to New York.
body: Two men accused of stabbing an off-duty New York City police detective in the Bronx were arrested in Lynn on Tuesday night, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, as reported by Boston.com.

According to the NYPD, the detective was stabbed several times and his chain was taken on Friday, Oct. 2. The two men were last seen fleeing on a motorized bike, police said. The NYPD identified them as Dangelo Caraballo and Sneider Mejia.

The case was referred to the U.S. Marshals Service NY/NJ Regional Fugitive Task Force, whose investigators learned the men had left the New York area together and tracked them to Massachusetts, Boston.com reported. A multi-agency operation took both into custody in Lynn.

Both men are being held by Massachusetts State Police while they await extradition to New York, according to the report. The specific charges and the detective's condition were not reported. Both men are presumed innocent.

Dennis Matulewicz, who leads the Marshals Service in the District of Massachusetts, called the stabbing an attack on every member of law enforcement and credited cooperation among federal, state and local agencies.

stories.title: One Person Shot Overnight Near Central Square in Cambridge
stories.dek: Cambridge police said the person was in stable condition and that there was no believed broader danger to the community.
body: One person was injured in a shooting near Central Square in Cambridge late Wednesday, Cambridge police said, according to Boston.com.
Shortly before midnight, authorities received a report of a person shot near Columbia Terrace, off Columbia Street, the Cambridge Police Department said in a Facebook post.
The person was taken to a local hospital, and police said Thursday that the victim was in stable condition with injuries that were not life-threatening. Police did not identify the person.

Police did not say whether a suspect had been identified or whether anyone had been arrested, Boston.com reported. The department said it does not believe there is any broader danger to the community.

The shooting remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact Cambridge detectives at 617-349-3300, and anonymous tips can be submitted by text or email following instructions on the department's website. Boston.com noted that one person was also injured in a separate shooting in North Cambridge on Tuesday.

stories.title: HONK! Fest, Free Museum Day Highlight Holiday Weekend Events
stories.dek: The Boston Globe's weekend guide for Oct. 9-12 included Somerville's street band festival, comedy, film screenings and free admission on Indigenous Peoples' Day.
body: Somerville's HONK! Fest, free museum admission on Indigenous Peoples' Day and a range of comedy, film and theater were among the events highlighted in the Boston Globe's guide to the weekend of Oct. 9 to 12.

HONK!, the 21st annual festival of activist street bands, ran Oct. 9 to 11, with Saturday performances centered on Davis Square and a Sunday parade from Davis Square to Harvard Square, according to the Globe. Harvard Square also hosted a Filipino American Festival on Oct. 10 with traditional dance and street food.
On Monday, Oct. 12, the Museum of Fine Arts and the Harvard Museums of Science & Culture offered free admission for Indigenous Peoples' Day, the Globe reported.

Comedy listings included Bobcat Goldthwait at The Comedy Studio in Cambridge on Oct. 9 and 10. Film picks included a live screening of Napoleon Dynamite with cast members at the Chevalier Theatre in Medford and selections from the IFFBoston Fall Focus series at the Brattle.

Theater recommendations included SpeakEasy Stage's Covenant, Lyric Stage Boston's All My Sons and CHUANG Stage's The Sitayana, according to the guide. The Boston Symphony Orchestra and the Boston Philharmonic both performed at Symphony Hall, and the Topsfield Fair closed Oct. 12.
