stories.title: Man Shot and Killed Inside Hyde Park Gas Station
stories.dek: Boston police said the shooting on Hyde Park Avenue did not appear to be random; no arrests had been made Wednesday evening.
body: A man was shot and killed inside a gas station and convenience store on Hyde Park Avenue on Wednesday evening, Boston police said, according to the Boston Globe.

Police received a report of a person shot at 5:09 p.m. at 1171 Hyde Park Ave., the Globe reported. Officers found a man inside with a gunshot wound, and he was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Speaking at the scene, Boston Police Superintendent Paul McLaughlin said the man was a customer in the store and that he and the shooter may have known each other, according to the Globe. McLaughlin said the shooting did not appear to be random and that detectives were canvassing the area for video and witnesses.

No arrests had been made, and the death had not yet been ruled a homicide, police said. If it is, it would be Boston's 25th homicide this year, according to police. Sgt. Det. John Boyle described the case as an active investigation.
Anyone with information is asked to call homicide detectives at 617-343-4470 or to call 1-800-494-TIPS anonymously.

stories.title: Fourth Person Charged in June Shooting in Mattapan That Killed One Man
stories.dek: Suffolk prosecutors charged a 19-year-old Jamaica Plain man with first-degree murder in the June 27 shooting on Blue Hill Avenue that also wounded four people.
body: A 19-year-old Jamaica Plain man has been charged with first-degree murder in a June shooting in Mattapan that killed a 26-year-old Brockton man and wounded four others, the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office said.

Cerrone Wilcox Buford was charged in Suffolk Superior Court with murder, armed assault to murder, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and several firearm offenses, according to the DA's office. He was ordered held without bail and is due back in court Nov. 3.

Prosecutors said a fight on June 27 began in the backyard of 1460 Blue Hill Ave. and moved to the sidewalk out front. According to prosecutors, video and witnesses show Wilcox Buford taking a gun from a bag and aiming it at the man, who was killed. At least seven shots were fired, and four people were wounded, the office said.

Three others have been charged, according to the release. Laquan Burris, 18, of Dorchester, and Javen Girault, 23, of Brockton, were ordered held on bail and are due back Nov. 3. An arrest warrant has been issued for Mannice Mitchner, 19, of Boston. Prosecutors said Burris, Girault and Mitchner were among those wounded. All are presumed innocent.
District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the case shows the harm illegal guns cause.

sources.title: Fourth person charged in June shooting that killed one man and injured four others

stories.title: Revere Man Arrested in Roxbury Stabbing After Knife Found on Rooftop
stories.dek: Boston police said detectives used video and evidence at the scene to identify a suspect in the Sept. 29 attack near Warren Street.
body: Boston police have arrested a 31-year-old Revere man in a stabbing in Roxbury last month, after detectives recovered what appeared to be the knife from a nearby rooftop, according to a department release.

Officers from District B-2 responded at about 7:12 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 29, to a report of a person stabbed near 301 Warren St., police said. After speaking with witnesses, officers followed evidence to a home on Kensington Park, where they found a 37-year-old man with a serious facial injury. He was taken to a local hospital, and his condition was not reported.

According to preliminary information, the two men had argued inside a nearby business, police said. Investigators believe the suspect followed the man outside and attacked him with a knife near Warren and Dale streets.

Detectives collected evidence at the scene and reviewed video from the business and nearby cameras to track the suspect's movements, according to the release. The next day, investigators found what appeared to be the knife on a rooftop and recovered it with help from the Boston Fire Department.

Police identified the suspect as Meshach Dowman, who is in custody and will be arraigned in Roxbury District Court on charges of assault with intent to murder, mayhem and assault and battery by means of a dangerous weapon. He is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Suspect Arrested in Roxbury Stabbing After Detectives Recover Knife from Rooftop

stories.title: Phoebe Bridgers Plays Phone-Free Show at TD Garden
stories.dek: Fans locked their phones in pouches for Bridgers' Oct. 6 Lost Tour stop, which a Boston.com reviewer praised for its staging and intimacy.
body: Phoebe Bridgers performed a phone-free concert at TD Garden on Tuesday, Oct. 6, on her Lost Tour supporting the album Lost Weekend, according to a review and setlist published by Boston.com. Alex G opened.

Attendees locked their phones in Yondr pouches after scanning their tickets, Boston.com reviewer Annie Jonas wrote, and the crowd watched without screens. Bridgers thanked fans for putting their phones away, according to the review.

The staging included a planetarium-style dome that rose to reveal Bridgers, her band and a string quartet, along with a large orb suspended over a second stage in the crowd, the review said. Bridgers performed the title track alone on that stage, and the quartet joined her for songs including "Graceland Too." Before "Still Standing," she spoke about her father's death.

The 23-song main set included "Motion Sickness," "Garden Song," "Kyoto" and "I Know the End," followed by an encore of a "Lost Weekend" reprise and "Scott Street," according to the setlist. The reviewer noted Massachusetts ties to the album, including a song named for the Liberty Tree Mall.

Jonas called the show carefully crafted and said Bridgers' intimacy carried over to an arena setting. Her criticisms were limited to the standard Boston greeting and some sports remarks by Alex G that she felt were ill-timed for a Boston audience.

sources.title: Review & setlist: Phoebe Bridgers brings phone-free, cosmic show to TD Garden
